title: [security] phase 5a reports CLEAN when a scanner fails — 10 sites, including all 3 GitHub alert queries
description:
Every security scanner in phase 5a reports CLEAN when it fails.

Ten call sites share the pattern:

  COUNT=$(tool ... 2>/dev/null | jq '...' || echo "0")
  if [[ "$COUNT" -gt 0 ]]; then  ...found...  else  ...no issues...  fi

Three things conspire, any one sufficient:
  1. 2>/dev/null discards the error, so a human reading the audit output
     never learns the tool complained
  2. || echo "0" substitutes a clean result for a failure
  3. even without (2), || binds to the PIPELINE. If the tool dies, jq gets
     empty input and emits nothing, so COUNT is "" -- and bash evaluates
     [[ "" -gt 0 ]] as false. Prints the checkmark.

DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-24, not inferred:
  GRYPE_COUNT=$(grype dir:/nonexistent-path-xyz --output json 2>/dev/null \
                 | jq '.matches | length' || echo "0")
  -> GRYPE_COUNT=[]  ->  "  OK Grype: No vulnerabilities"

Found because cachyos-sentinel's target/ had grown to 46 GB, which made
grype exceed 3 minutes and get killed. Phase 5a reported that project
grype-clean without grype ever completing a scan.

THE TEN SITES (line numbers at 02d8db8):
  159 DEPENDABOT_COUNT   open Dependabot alerts
  168 CODE_COUNT         open CodeQL alerts
  177 SECRET_COUNT       open secret-scanning alerts
  246 BANDIT_HIGH        Python high-severity
  259 SEMGREP_COUNT      semgrep
  278 CODEQL_ISSUES      local CodeQL SARIF
  316 TRIVY_VULNS        trivy vuln+secret
  328 GRYPE_COUNT        grype
  368 VULN_TOTAL         npm audit
  415 CHECKOV_FAILED     IaC misconfig

The first three are the worst: they are gh api calls, and they are what
enforces the mandatory rule in security.md that ALL GitHub security alerts
be resolved or documented. An expired token, a rate limit, a network blip,
or a repo the token cannot see all return "0 open alerts" and the audit
proceeds as though the baseline were met.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW: the code is idiomatic defensive bash. It reads as
careful error handling. It is the command-v guard's evil twin -- a MISSING
tool being skipped is defensible; a PRESENT tool failing and being reported
clean is worse, because you believe you ran it.

OPERATOR DECISIONS 2026-08-24:
  scope     -- fix all ten, via one shared helper, so an eleventh scanner is
               correct by default
  behaviour -- a failed scanner prints its real stderr, counts toward
               TOTAL_ISSUES, and reports "result UNKNOWN", never clean
  history   -- re-run phase 5a on the active projects once fixed
  timing    -- fix now, before cachyos-sentinel phase 1 starts
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-24 — both halves. 17 sites total.

phase-5a (10 sites): scan_count + scan_failed. Keys on PARSEABILITY, not the
exit code, because bandit/semgrep/checkov/npm-audit all exit non-zero when
they FIND things.

phase-9d (7 sites): gh_json + json_count + audit_unknown.

CORRECTION to this issue's original description, measured rather than
reasoned. The 9d sites went wrong TWO different ways, and only one of them
was the false clean I first described:

  empty stdout (network failure, gh crash, timeout, killed process)
    jq emits nothing, COUNT becomes "", [[ "" -eq 0 ]] is TRUE
    -> "No open alerts". FALSE CLEAN. This is the dangerous one.

  HTTP error carrying a JSON body (401 Bad credentials, 404 Not Found)
    gh writes the error object to STDOUT, so `jq length` counts its KEYS
    -> "3 open alert(s)". PHANTOM ALERTS, and the detail render then
    prints nothing because .[] does not apply to an object.

So an expired token did NOT produce a false clean here; it produced three
imaginary alerts. My earlier note on this issue said otherwise and was
wrong. The 5a half was characterised correctly: those run the tool
directly, the error goes to stderr, stdout is empty, and the result is a
false clean.

Also fixed in passing, same class:
  git rev-list --count ... || echo "0"  (x2) -- a failure made both counts
  zero, which renders as "In sync with remote": a false clean about push
  state, from the step that exists to check push state.
  FAILED_RUNS -- how the audit learns CI is red. A gh failure reported zero
  failed runs: the 95-red-commits incident class, made invisible by the
  check meant to catch it.

TESTS: tests/test-scan-count.sh and tests/test-gh-json.sh, 9 cases each.
Both EXTRACT the helpers from the skill documents, so they exercise
shipping code rather than a copy that can drift. Both were proven able to
fail -- restoring the old swallow turns the failure cases red, and
restoring an exit-code gate turns the nonzero-exit-with-findings case red.

Verified end to end against real gh: a 404 repo now reports
"FAILED - result UNKNOWN, NOT clean / gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)" and counts
an issue; an invalid token reports "gh: Bad credentials (HTTP 401)"; a real
repo still returns count=0 correctly.

REMAINING: re-run phase 5a and 9d against the active projects, per the
operator decision of 2026-08-24. Not yet done.
